public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 459

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/459](https://www.erdosproblems.com/459)
- [ErGr80] P. Erdős and R. L. Graham, *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*, Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique 28 (1980), p.91.
- [OEIS A289280](https://oeis.org/A289280)
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace Erdos459

/--
The function from the problem, in its equivalent form: `f u` is the smallest `v > u` all of whose
prime factors divide `u`. (Equivalently, `f u` is the largest `v` such that no `m ∈ (u, v)` is
composed entirely of primes dividing `u * v`.)
-/
noncomputable def f (u : ℕ) : ℕ := sInf {v | u < v ∧ v.primeFactors ⊆ u.primeFactors}

/--
Let $f(u)$ be the largest $v$ such that no $m\in (u,v)$ is composed entirely of primes dividing
$uv$. Estimate $f(u)$.

The estimate $u + 2 \le f(u) \le u^2$ holds for every $u \ge 2$. The upper bound is attained
when $u$ is prime, and the lower bound when $u = 2^k - 2$ with $k \ge 2$; Cambie further showed
that $f(n) = (1 + o(1))n$ for almost all $n$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Woett/Lean-files/blob/main/ErdosProblem459.lean"]
theorem erdos_459 {u : ℕ} (hu : 2 ≤ u) : u + 2 ≤ f u ∧ f u ≤ u ^ 2 := by
  sorry

/--
The upper bound $f u ≤ u ^ 2$ is attained exactly when `u` is prime: $f p = p ^ 2$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Woett/Lean-files/blob/main/ErdosProblem459.lean"]
theorem erdos_459.variants.upper_tight {p : ℕ} (hp : p.Prime) : f p = p ^ 2 := by
  sorry

end Erdos459

findings.description: The main theorem states only `2 ≤ u → u + 2 ≤ f u ∧ f u ≤ u ^ 2`. The source calls these bounds trivial, and they are not the recorded answer to "Estimate f(u)". The site marks the problem solved because of Cambie's observations: (i) both bounds are attained infinitely often, with f(p)=p² for primes and f(2^k−2)=2^k for k≥2, and (ii) f(n)=(1+o(1))n for almost all n. The file formalizes only half of (i), as `erdos_459.variants.upper_tight`. The lower-bound sharpness and the almost-all asymptotic have no Lean statement, even though the theorem's docstring asserts both. So the `research solved` main statement is strictly weaker than the resolution the source records. The statement is true and faithful to the part it covers (I proved it in Lean in about 20 lines), so this is incomplete rather than wrong. For an open-ended "estimate" problem, stating the trivial bounds is a defensible but debatable choice. Other solved "Estimate" files here (e.g. 648, 1025, 1188) state the substantive estimate.
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/459 (Wayback snapshot 2026-08-24): "In particular, we trivially have u+2≤f(u)≤u^2. Cambie has noted that when u=p is a prime, f(p)=p^2 ... In particular, f(u)=u+2 whenever u=2^k−2 for k≥2. In particular the function f(u) does not exhibit any regular growth, since there are infinitely many u such that f(u)=u+2 and infinitely many u such that f(u)=u^2. Cambie can also show that f(n)=(1+o(1))n for almost all n. ... Since Cambie's observations seem to settle the most obvious questions, I will mark this as solved." Forum thread 459: BorisAlexeev: "I have formalized SOME of the results ... I consider this NOT complete ... The missing result is f(n)=(1+o(1))n for almost all n." StijnC: "If one aims for the typical behaviour, the answer is that f(n) ∼ n most of the time." The site moved to SOLVED (LEAN) only after Woett/Aristotle formalized the almost-all result.
findings.suggested_fix:
Keep `erdos_459` as it is, and add the missing parts of the recorded resolution as variants (both typecheck against the file; I proved the first in a few lines):
`theorem erdos_459.variants.lower_tight {k : ℕ} (hk : 2 ≤ k) : f (2 ^ k - 2) = 2 ^ k`
`theorem erdos_459.variants.almost_all {ε : ℝ} (hε : 0 < ε) : {n : ℕ | (1 + ε) * (n : ℝ) ≤ f n}.HasDensity 0`
Both are proved in the linked Woett file (`f_eq_u_plus_two_of_u_eq_pow_two_sub_two`, `main_theorem`). Alternatively, make the main theorem the conjunction of the bounds, their sharpness, and the almost-all statement.

findings.description: The docstring says "The upper bound f u ≤ u^2 is attained exactly when u is prime". Under the usual reading of "exactly when", that is `f u = u^2 ↔ u.Prime`. The Lean states only one direction, `p.Prime → f p = p ^ 2`. The converse is true: I proved in Lean that for u ≥ 2 not prime, f u ≤ u·minFac u < u², and OEIS A289280 records a(n) ≤ n·lpf(n). But the Lean does not state the converse, and the source does not claim it. The mathematics of the statement is correct. The docstring just claims more than the theorem says. ("attained exactly" could also be read as "attained with equality", which lowers confidence.)
findings.source_evidence: erdosproblems.com/459: "Cambie has noted that when u=p is a prime, f(p)=p^2". This is one direction only, and it matches the Lean. OEIS A289280 FORMULA: "For any n > 1, n < a(n) <= n*lpf(n)", which gives the converse.
findings.suggested_fix: Either change the docstring to "The upper bound $f(u) \le u^2$ is attained when $u$ is prime: $f(p) = p^2$.", or strengthen the statement to `theorem ... {u : ℕ} (hu : 2 ≤ u) : f u = u ^ 2 ↔ u.Prime` (both directions are provable).

reformulations.difference: The source defines f(u) as the largest v such that no m ∈ (u, v) is composed entirely of primes dividing uv. The Lean instead defines `f u = sInf {v | u < v ∧ v.primeFactors ⊆ u.primeFactors}`, the smallest v > u all of whose prime factors divide u. This is the "equivalent definition" given on erdosproblems.com.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Take u ≥ 2. The set is nonempty because u² is in it, so g := f u is in the set. g satisfies the literal condition: if u < m < g and every prime of m divides u·g, then every prime of m divides u (the primes of g already divide u), so m is a smaller element of the set, which is impossible. Every v > g fails the condition: m = g lies in (u, v), and all its primes divide u, which divides uv. So g is the largest v. I proved this in Lean as `IsGreatest {v : ℕ | ∀ m, u < m → m < v → ¬ m.primeFactors ⊆ (u * v).primeFactors} (f u)` under `2 ≤ u`. Outside that domain the values are junk and neither theorem reaches them, since both need u ≥ 2: f 0 = 1 and f 1 = sInf ∅ = 0 (for u = 1 the source's "largest v" does not exist). The values also match OEIS A289280 (offset 2) on every computed term.

review.notes:
What I checked:
- Both theorem statements are true. I proved each in a scratch file in about 20 lines. This fits the source, which calls the bounds trivial and credits f(p)=p² to Cambie.
- The theorems require u ≥ 2 (resp. p prime), so the junk values f 0 = 1 and f 1 = 0 are never reached.
- Status: `research solved` matches the site ("SOLVED (LEAN)", last updated 2026-03-11 in teorth/erdosproblems). There is no status issue.
- `formal_proof`: the linked Woett file contains no `sorry`. Its `f_bounds` and `f_prime` have the same statements as `erdos_459` and `upper_tight`. Its `f` (`if u < 2 then 0 else Nat.find …`) agrees with the file's `sInf` definition for u ≥ 2 and differs only at u = 0. The link points to the mutable `main` branch rather than a pinned commit. That is a maintenance matter, not a mathematical one.
- References: the module docstring's [ErGr80, p.91] citation is correct. I confirmed the problem text on book page 91 of the scan.

Remaining observation (not reported as a finding): the main theorem is a trivially true fact tagged `research solved`. That tag reflects the problem's status, so I only folded it into the "questionable" finding about incompleteness.
